outcomes: An engine, a credential provider and an extension exchange registry credentials, publication ops and uploads through one versioned, strictly parsed contract, pinned with its schema and fixtures
A bearer reaches only the hosts its credential names, is fetched once per purpose while it is valid, and is never printed
A provider that echoes publication-v1 and uploader-v1 publishes a plan and uploads its members with a credential it holds itself, so no publish credential crosses a repository process
nonGoals: Which processes enable the provider and when it starts, which the CLI's credential-provider feature owns
How the engine plans, uploads and releases a publication, which the CLI's provider-publication feature owns
How a provider obtains its credentials and which registries it serves, which each provider owns
The release-set documents inside resolve and release, which the distribution protocol owns

requirements.text: The seam version is 1. An extension finds the CLI in PUTNAMI_CLI_EXECUTABLE and runs cloud registry-token --host <host>; materialize is the seam's other flag, and publish-provider stays a reserved name. The SDK resolver (tooling/extension-sdk) passes the host and nothing else, runs the advertised CLI without a relaunch through the workspace pin, and answers nothing for an empty host.

A seam token is valid only when it is not empty and holds no whitespace. The SDK resolver returns the whole settled bearer without its newline. It reads an answer with whitespace as no token, with a hint; a failed command as no token, with the command's stderr as the hint; and empty stdout or a missing CLI as no token and no hint.

The provider serves the reserved command credential-provider, which is not the publish-provider name. The RPC version is 1 and its capability is credential-v1. The purposes are read and publish and no other, and the ops are initialize, credential and shutdown.

A provider answers initialize with the RPC version and the capabilities it echoes, acknowledges shutdown with an empty answer, and exits when its stdin reaches EOF, whether or not it received shutdown. The Cloud provider (cloud/extension) does so, and without a run credential it echoes credential-v1 alone.

Every valid fixture line parses and re-encodes byte for byte, and every invalid one is refused. The credential parsers refuse malformed payloads, a duplicate member, nesting past the bound, a line over 64 KiB, invalid UTF-8, an answer to an unknown op and a shutdown answer with a payload. The Cloud provider refuses a request before initialize, a second initialize, an unknown op, an unknown or wrong-case member, another purpose and another version, and ends the session on a line over the bound.

The JSON Schema schemas/credential-provider-v1.json holds the members, required lists, closed objects, enums, bounds and grammars of the Go contract, the upload definitions included. Evaluated with the schema, every valid fixture passes and every invalid one fails, except those whose rule the schema names inexpressible. Its run-credential grammar refuses exactly the runes unicode.IsSpace reports.

A credential has a printable ASCII bearer of at most 16 KiB, an expiry in RFC 3339 UTC ending in Z, and 1 to 64 valid hosts, none with a trailing dot or an IPv6 address. It serves an https URL, or http to loopback, without userinfo, whose host and port match an entry, an entry without a port naming the default port; it serves nothing else, and nothing for an invalid entry. The CLI (tooling/cli) serves its bearer only to such a URL.

A credential and a credential response never print the bearer under %v, %+v, %s or %#v. Initialize params never print the run credential, which the wire still carries, and say runCredential:<redacted> when one is present; an invalid run credential is refused without being quoted. Publication request and response lines print none of their payload.
A run credential is valid UTF-8 of 1 to 16 KiB with no rune that unicode.IsSpace reports, so a no-break or an ideographic space is refused.

The provider is the one loaded extension that declares the credential-provider command. Two declaring extensions fail the first request that needs a credential, not the start of the process. The CLI builds its provider broker for two declaring extensions and fails the first credential request with ErrProviderAmbiguous.

An engine asks at most once per purpose while the answer is valid, across every host and concurrent request, and renews a credential before it expires by the smaller of one minute and half its lifetime. The CLI makes one call per purpose for 48 concurrent requests to 6 URLs, renews a 10-minute credential 1 minute early and a 30-second one at 15 seconds, and refuses an expired one. The Cloud provider shares one Delivery call among concurrent requests of a purpose.

A refusal fails every request of its purpose, whatever its host, with its code, and absence serves nothing; both hold for the rest of the process. The CLI asks a refusal once and fails every later request of its purpose, on any host, with its code, and asks an absence once. The Cloud provider answers the publish purpose with absence, an empty payload, and asks Delivery nothing for it.

A provider that cannot start, crashes, answers out of protocol or does not answer in time fails the request. The failure answers for 30 seconds, and the first request after that starts the provider again. The CLI fails the request on a malformed answer, a hang or a failed start, starts a crashed, hung or unstartable provider once within the backoff, and starts it again after.

publication-v1 holds only when the engine offers it and the provider echoes it; without it both sides refuse resolve, open and release, while initialize, credential and shutdown hold in every session. The CLI offers credential-v1, publication-v1 and uploader-v1, and sends no open after a credential-v1 echo. The Cloud provider echoes publication-v1 only on a hosted run offered it, with a Delivery base and valid origins; otherwise it refuses resolve and calls no Delivery route.

publication-v1 adds the ops resolve, open and release. Its refusal codes are plan_not_open, plan_already_open, plan_mismatch, artifact_missing, artifact_digest_mismatch, not_forward, conflict, channel_immutable and namespace_forbidden. A plan is version 1 and at most 1 MiB, and an ancestry snapshot holds at most 1,000,000 commits.

A resolve, open or release line is at most 8 MiB and 12 levels deep, while initialize, credential and shutdown lines keep 64 KiB and 5 levels in every session. Once publication-v1 is negotiated, the Cloud provider reads a resolve line past 64 KiB whole and ends the session on a line past 8 MiB.

A plan encodes to the bytes of the release plan contract, and its digest is the sha256 of that encoding without planDigest, pinned by a test vector. Its members are in (ecosystem, coordinate) order, and the order changes the digest. A plan may select Put registry members, of the archive and put ecosystems, and its release names an evidence digest for each, equal to the member's artifact digest.

A release payload's request is the distribution release request byte for byte and normalizes as distribution does, and the resolve and release fixtures form distribution exchanges. A null is left to distribution only inside the request member, and refused anywhere else.

The validators refuse a plan of another version, without a channel or with a duplicate one, with an unlisted immutable channel, a duplicate member, a foreign source revision or the digest of another plan; an ancestry with a malformed source, snapshot or channel list, or an ancestor with no head; and evidence that is unsorted, duplicated, malformed or over 4 MiB. The publication payload parsers refuse malformed input and a resolve by releaseId.

Open is idempotent on the plan digest, and another plan in the same session gets plan_already_open. A plan is released at most once, and another release set for it gets plan_mismatch. The CLI opens the same plan again with the first answer, names a refused plan, and sends a release whose answer was lost once more, which the provider applies once. The Cloud provider opens a plan once through Delivery and answers another set with plan_mismatch.

Before open, a release is refused with plan_not_open, and so is an upload. After an open refused with not_forward, the CLI names the plan digest, uploads nothing, refuses an upload with plan_not_open, sends no release and moves no channel. The Cloud provider refuses a release before open with plan_not_open.

uploader-v1 holds only beside publication-v1: an initialize that names it without publication-v1 is refused, and upload, request and answer, is allowed only in a session that negotiated both. The Cloud provider echoes uploader-v1 only when the engine offers it beside publication-v1 on a hosted run with origins, and refuses an upload in a session that did not negotiate it, before any registry request.

uploader-v1 adds the op upload, with an 8 MiB line, a registry of at most 2,048 bytes and an outbox of at most 4,096 bytes. Its refusal codes are plan_not_open, plan_mismatch, registry_not_served, artifact_digest_mismatch, artifact_conflict and upload_failed.

An upload request holds planDigest, registry, outbox, kind and member, and no credential; its answer holds digest and platforms, and no reuse flag. No answer or diagnostic of the Cloud provider carries the plan's bearer.

An upload names an https registry, or http to loopback, without userinfo, fragment or trailing slash, and an absolute outbox without a . or .. segment; the kind matches the member, and no error repeats the registry. An answer is a sha256 digest, with platforms absent or 1 to 32 lowercase os/arch pairs. An upload line has the publication bounds, and each invalid upload fixture fails for the rule its name states.

An upload is refused before open with plan_not_open and for another plan or a member the plan does not select with plan_mismatch. The Cloud provider refuses those, registry_not_served for a registry outside its origins, even the same host at another port, and a bearer Delivery will not renew, before any registry request. It answers a tampered artifact with artifact_digest_mismatch, another artifact at the version with artifact_conflict and any other failure with upload_failed.
